old_setup.description: An old version of the FMI integration is already in use. You can move the old setup, with its history, straight to the new version. You can also set up the new version beside the old one.

menu_options.move: Move the old setup to the new version

user.title: FMI Open Data
user.description: Choose the language FMI Open Data uses. The choice affects the query and parameter names shown when adding measurements, the language of the data FMI returns, and the language of warning texts.

reconfigure.title: FMI Open Data
reconfigure.description: Choose the language FMI Open Data uses. The choice applies to every station and place.

init.title: Stale data
init.description:
When a sensor's newest data is older than this, the binary sensor for stale data turns on, and a repair issue can tell you what is wrong.

The setting applies to every sensor. Daily, monthly and yearly statistics are only reported once the period is over, so for those the limit is never shorter than three days, two months or two years.

data.no_data_issue: Raise a repair issue when a sensor stops getting data
data.no_data_issue_hours: Hours without new data before the data is considered stale

error.no_parameters: Choose at least one thing to measure.

error.no_data: FMI returned no data for this place. Check the place and try again.
error.keep_one: At least one measurement has to stay. The whole station can be removed on the integration page.

user.title: What do you want to measure?
user.description: Choose one or more. Search by name, such as rain or snow. The stations are chosen in the next step.

station.title: Station
station.description: Where is {measurement} read? Nearest first. Listed are the stations that have reported this measurement recently.

data.show_all: Show all of the query's stations

data_description.show_all: Also the stations that have not reported this measurement recently.

data_description.place_name: Shown as the device's name, in front of the measurement sensors' names.

named_place.title: Place
named_place.description: This query has no stations. Type the name of the place {measurement} is read for, such as Kotka.

names.title: Names
names.description: The names are filled in. Home Assistant shows the station's name in front of the sensors' names. The names can be changed in Home Assistant later.

add_measurements.title: Add measurements
add_measurements.description: Only the data the station measures is listed.

data.negative_as_zero: Report -1 as 0. Helpful with parameters that return -1 when there is no measurable value, such as precipitation on days when it has not rained.
data.forecast_step: Time step between two forecast values in minutes

data_description.unit: If you leave the field empty, FMI's own unit is used. It is not available for every parameter.

remove_measurements.title: Remove measurements
remove_measurements.description: The entities of the removed measurements are removed.

error.nothing_followed: Choose the weather forecast, warning types or both.
error.no_forecast: FMI has no forecast for this place. Pick a place in Finland or nearby.

user.title: Place
user.description:
Pick the place on the map. A warning is included when its area covers the chosen place, or comes within the circle's radius.

On an island or by the shore, a radius of a kilometre or two makes sure the warnings for the nearby sea area are included.

data_description.label: The place's name. Home Assistant shows it in front of the entities' names.
data_description.weather: The weather entity shows FMI's forecast for it, hour by hour for about nine days, and by day and by half day.
data_description.warning_types: Empty means no warnings are followed.

options.sea_thunderstorm: Severe thunderstorm warning for sea areas

parameter_missing.title: FMI measurement {label} no longer gets data
parameter_missing.description:
The station ({target_type} {target}) no longer reports "{parameter}", so the measurement has no value.

The station currently reports {available}.

Remove the measurement from the station, and add one of these if you like.

no_data.title: FMI measurement {label} no longer gets data
no_data.description:
The query {query_id} returns nothing at all for {target_type} {target}.

The station may have been decommissioned or renumbered, or it may no longer serve this query. Remove the measurement, and add it again at a station that has it.

old_folder.title: Delete the old FMI folder
old_folder.description: FMI is now FMI Open Data, and its old folder {path} is no longer used. Delete the folder and restart Home Assistant.

get_observations.name: Get observations
get_observations.description: Gets one station's observations over a chosen time range straight from FMI, without a sensor for each value.

query.name: Query
query.description: The ID of an FMI observation query, such as fmi::observations::weather::hourly.

parameters.name: Parameters
parameters.description: The parameters of the query to get, such as TA_PT1H_AVG.

start.name: Start
start.description: The start of the time range. By default 24 hours before the end.

end.name: End
end.description: The end of the time range. By default now.

timestep.name: Step
timestep.description: The time between values. By default the query's own.

not_loaded.message: FMI Open Data is not set up.

not_an_observation_query.message: {query} is not an FMI observation query.

start_after_end.message: The start of the time range must be before the end of the time range.

no_observations.message: FMI has no observations for this query, station and time range.

refused.message: FMI refused the request with the message "{message}".
